title: Land, Sea and Sky! Helicopter, Boat and Rocket for Kids
intro: Hi, friends! I'm Bolt the little tow truck, and welcome to Tiny Truck Town!
Today we're meeting five vehicles that go on land, on water and in the sky.
Can you count them with me? One, two, three, four, five!
Some fly, one floats, and some roll along! Let's find out.

lines: Here's our first stop. Here's a clue: it has long blades that spin on top! Can you guess?
A helicopter is a flying machine.
The blades on top are called a rotor. They spin super fast to lift it up.
It can fly up, down, forward and even backward!
Can you spin your arm like a rotor? Whirr, whirr!
Can you guess what the little rotor on the tail does?
It keeps the helicopter from spinning around and around!
One more time, nice and loud: HELICOPTER!
Helicopters can hover, staying still in one spot in the sky.
Who's next? Here's a clue: it's bright orange and it floats on the water! Can you guess?
A rescue boat helps keep people safe on the water.
It moves fast through the waves and leaves a white trail.
Its crew practices every day, so they are always ready.
Can you make waves with your arms? Swoosh, swoosh!
Can you guess why rescue boats are bright orange?
Orange is super easy to see on blue water!
Let's say it together: RESCUE BOAT!
One more time, nice and loud: RESCUE BOAT!
It carries life rings and life jackets. On a boat, we always wear a life jacket.
Who's next? Here's a clue: it's small, but it pushes giant airplanes! Can you guess?
An airplane tug works at the airport.
A strong bar connects the tug to the airplane's front wheel.
It's low and flat, so it fits under the airplane's nose.
Can you push like a tug? Push, push!
Can you guess why big airplanes need a tug?
They don't back up by themselves at the gate, so the tug pushes them back!
Let's say it together: AIRPLANE TUG!
One more time, nice and loud: AIRPLANE TUG!
Small but mighty! Tugs are super strong.
Who's next? Here's a clue: it carries a rocket to the launch pad! Can you guess?
A rocket mover carries a giant rocket.
Some rockets lie down for the ride, then stand up tall at the launch pad.
Rockets carry astronauts and satellites into space.
Can you count down with me? Three, two, one, blast off!
Can you guess how fast a giant rocket mover goes?
Very slowly! Some go slower than you can walk.
Let's say it together: ROCKET MOVER!
One more time, nice and loud: ROCKET MOVER!
Going slowly keeps the rocket safe and steady.
Who's last? Here's a clue: it rolls on tracks and says choo choo! Can you guess?
A train travels on long metal tracks.
The engine pulls lots of cars behind it.
Some trains carry people, and some carry cargo, like wood and grain.
Can you chug your arms like a train? Choo choo!
Can you guess why trains blow their horns?
To say, here I come! Toot, toot!
One more time, nice and loud: TRAIN!
Train wheels have special edges that keep them on the rails.

recap: The helicopter's tail rotor stops it from spinning.
The rescue boat is orange, so it's easy to see.
The tug pushes airplanes back from the gate.
The rocket mover goes slow and steady.
And the train toots its horn!
outro: Which one would you like to ride? Be kind, and wave hello to the vehicles you see.
Bye, friends! See you in Tiny Truck Town!
